coverage_notes:
SCOPE. Anchor snapshot of the FTSE 100 as at 19 December 2005 (the effective date of the December 2005
annual review) plus every constituent change from then to 22 June 2026 (the June 2026 annual review). 161 dated
entries: 140 change membership (78 on quarterly/annual review effective dates, 62 ad-hoc - acquisitions, schemes of
arrangement, demergers, suspensions and nationality reassignments between reviews) and 21 are name/ticker changes that
carry no membership change (see RENAMES below). Four review quarters in the span
produced no FTSE 100 change at all and therefore have no entry: 2006-Q1, 2018-Q3, 2023-Q1 and 2025-Q2; the first was
confirmed against the FTSE Russell review spreadsheet, the last two against LSEG press releases, and 2018-Q3 against
contemporaneous constituent lists.

EFFECTIVE-DATE CONVENTION (verified). FTSE Russell review notices state the convention explicitly, e.g. the March 2005
notice: "All constituent changes will be applied after the close of business on Friday, 18 March 2005 and will be
effective on Monday, 21 March 2005". The `effective` field in this file is FTSE Russell's stated effective date, i.e.
the FIRST TRADING DAY on which the new constituent list applies - the Monday after the third Friday of March, June,
September and December. A backtest that rebalances on `effective` is trading the new membership on its first day, not
before it. Exactly one review in this span departs from the rule: the March 2008 review was applied after the close on
Tuesday 25 March and took effect on Wednesday 26 March 2008, because the third Friday of March 2008 (21 March) was Good
Friday. Every other review effective date in the file is a Monday falling after the third Friday of its month, and a
validation assertion checks both properties. Every review effective date here was read from the text of the
corresponding FTSE Russell notice, never inferred from a calendar rule.

SOURCES, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT.
(1) FTSE Russell, "FTSE 100 - Historic Additions and Deletions", April 2026 edition
    (https://www.lseg.com/content/dam/ftse-russell/en_us/documents/policy-documents/ftse-100-constituent-history.pdf).
    This is the index owner's own dated add/delete register back to 1984 and is the spine of the `changes` array.
(2) FTSE Russell index notices (research.ftserussell.com/products/index-notices), used for EVERY review effective date
    in the file and for each ad-hoc event listed as a correction below. These are the primary announcements.
(3) FTSE Russell per-review spreadsheets (FTSE_UK_Review.xls / .xlsx), recovered from Internet Archive captures of
    www.ftse.com, giving the FTSE 100 Inclusions/Exclusions tables with SEDOLs. Available and used for the June 2005
    to September 2013 reviews (with gaps at March 2008, September 2011, September and December 2012, and March, June
    and December 2013) and for March 2016, December 2017 and March 2018.
(4) LSEG press releases for the March 2019 to June 2026 reviews.
Wikipedia revisions of the "FTSE 100 Index" article were used only as an independent cross-check on constituent lists
at points in time, and to identify the replacement constituent in two ad-hoc events where the FTSE Russell notice did
not name it; they are never the sole source for a change.

WHERE THE INDEX OWNER'S OWN DOCUMENT IS WRONG OR INCOMPLETE - READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING IT.
Replaying source (1) alone does not conserve the constituent count. Twelve events in this span are missing from it or
recorded incorrectly, and each has been repaired here against the specific FTSE Russell notice named in the entry's
`source`:
  * 2009-01-09  British Energy Group out / Pennon Group in   - missing from (1); notice 344671
  * 2009-01-19  HBOS out / Balfour Beatty in                  - missing from (1); notice 344637
  * 2009-11-05  Friends Provident out / Resolution in         - missing from (1); notice 343198
  * 2010-02-08  Cadbury out / ARM Holdings in                 - missing from (1); notice 342750
  * 2010-09-24  Tomkins out / GKN in                          - missing from (1); notice 341664
  * 2013-05-01  Xstrata out / William Hill in                 - missing from (1); notice 337232
  * 2016-10-05  SABMiller out / Croda International in        - missing from (1); notice 1764665
  * 2019-10-21/23 M&G in, then Just Eat out on re-ranking     - missing from (1); notices 2594263 and 2594312
  * 2023-04-20/25 Dowlais Group in, then out on re-ranking    - (1) shows Melrose Industries deleted on 20 April 2023,
      which is wrong (Melrose remained a constituent), and shows Dowlais as an addition on both dates; notices 2607680
      and 2607713
  * 2015-03-23  Hikma Pharmaceuticals in / Tullow Oil out     - (1) dates this 20 March 2015, the Friday on which the
      change was applied at the close; notice 1328995 gives the effective date as Monday 23 March 2015
  * 2010-03-22/26/30 Cable & Wireless plc renamed Cable & Wireless Communications, then Cable & Wireless Worldwide
      added on demerger and Cable & Wireless Communications deleted on re-ranking - the whole sequence is missing from
      (1); notices 342656, 342487 and 342467
  * 2018-10-12  Sky out / Wood Group (John) in                 - the date cell for this row in (1) is typeset
      '12- Oct-18' with a space inside the date, which naive extraction silently attaches to the preceding row's date
      (28 June 2018). The date here is read as 12 October 2018, consistent with Comcast's acquisition of Sky
(1) also misspells Renishaw as 'Reinshaw' in its rows of 22 March 2021 and 21 June 2021; the name is corrected here.
Also removed: a duplicate NMC Health deletion dated 27 April 2020 in (1). NMC Health was removed from the FTSE 100 at
the March 2020 review (effective 23 March 2020) while suspended; the April notice (2596168) is the formality that
completed its removal from the wider FTSE UK series after 40 days of suspension, not a second FTSE 100 deletion.
The consequence for a user of this file: the LSEG PDF is authoritative on the events it records but demonstrably not
complete, so any independent reconciliation against it will show these differences. They are ours, and they are sourced.

CONSTITUENT COUNT AND THE 101 EXCEPTION. The replay holds at exactly 100 companies on every date in the span except
during four documented demerger windows, when an ELIGIBLE demerged company is admitted immediately and the smallest
constituent is removed a few trading days later after re-ranking, leaving the index at 101 companies in between:
  2010-03-26 to 2010-03-29 (Cable & Wireless Worldwide / Cable & Wireless Communications), 2019-10-21 to 2019-10-22
  (M&G / Prudential), 2022-07-18 to 2022-07-20 (Haleon / GSK) and 2023-04-20 to 2023-04-24 (Dowlais Group / Melrose
  Industries). Each is sourced to the FTSE Russell notice that created it; the 2010 window is the clearest, its notice
  stating in terms 'Please note: There will be 101 companies in the FTSE 100'.

TEMPORARY DEMERGER LINES ARE NOT MEMBERSHIP, AND ARE EXCLUDED. Separately from the four windows above, FTSE Russell
sometimes inserts a temporary line representing an entitlement to shares in a company that is INELIGIBLE for the FTSE
UK Index Series - because it is foreign-incorporated, standard-listed or listed abroad - purely so that the demerger
is market-capitalisation neutral, and deletes it days later. Four such lines appear in the LSEG register in this span
and are DELIBERATELY NOT recorded here as membership, on the same principle that excludes second share lines:
Thungela Resources (7-11 June 2021, 'Standard listed and ineligible for inclusion within the FTSE UK Index Series',
notice 2600397), Jackson Financial 'dummy line' (1-22 September 2021, 'a temporary line representing the Jackson
Financial shares will be added to the same indices as Prudential (including the FTSE 100 Index) at an estimated
valuation, with the event being market capitalisation neutral', notice 2601225), the Valterra Platinum distribution
line (2-5 June 2025, FTSE nationality South Africa, notice 2615948) and The Magnum Ice Cream Company (8-11 December
2025, FTSE nationality Netherlands, notice 2617955). Recording them would put a non-member in the universe and would
show the index at 101 for three weeks in September 2021, which is what an earlier revision of this file did.

SHARE LINES VERSUS COMPANIES. This file models COMPANY membership, so the anchor is 100 companies and the replay holds
at 100 companies. The FTSE 100 has carried MORE THAN 100 SECURITY LINES for most of this period, and a security-level
universe will not agree with this file. Royal Dutch Shell A and B were both constituents from 20 July 2005 until the
share-structure simplification effective 31 January 2022; Schroders carried a voting and a non-voting line, and the
FTSE Russell June 2012 review spreadsheet lists both "Schroders N/V" and Man Group as FTSE 100 exclusions where the
LSEG register lists only Man Group. The Wikipedia revision used for the anchor states in terms that in December 2005
there were "100 companies, but a total of 102 listings". Share-line events are NOT recorded as changes here because no
company entered or left the index: the 31 January 2022 deletion of the Royal Dutch Shell B line is present in the LSEG
register and is deliberately omitted from `changes`, and the June 2012 Schroders N/V exclusion is likewise omitted. A
consumer needing security-level membership must add these separately.

RENAMES. A change entry may carry a `renamed` list ({from_ticker, to_ticker, new_name}) instead of, or alongside,
added/removed. A rename continues the same membership under a new ticker and does not alter the constituent count; the
replay splits the spell at the ticker boundary so that ticker+date resolution works either side of it. This file
carries 24 rename records, each with its own citation in the entry's `source`: Hilton Group/HG. to Ladbrokes/LAD
(2006-02-22), Boots Group/BOOT to Alliance Boots/AB. (2006-07-31), Cable & Wireless/CW. to Cable & Wireless
Communications/CWC (2010-03-22), Slough Estates/SLOU to SEGRO/SGRO (2007, date
approximate), AMVESCAP/AVZ to Invesco/IVZ (2007-05-24), Reuters Group/RTR to Thomson Reuters/TRIL (2008-04-17),
Liberty International/LII to Capital Shopping Centres/CSCG (2010-05-07), British Airways/BAY to International
Consolidated Airlines Group/IAG (2011-01-24), CSCG to Intu Properties/INTU (2013-02-18), Resolution/RSL to Friends
Life Group/FLG (May 2014, day approximate), British Sky Broadcasting/BSY to Sky/SKY (2014-11-21), Imperial Tobacco/IMT
to Imperial Brands/IMB (2016-02-08), Wolseley/WOS to Ferguson/FERG (2017-07-31), Standard Life/SL. to Standard Life
Aberdeen/SLA (2017-08-14), BHP Billiton/BLT to BHP Group/BHP (2018-11-23), Paddy Power Betfair/PPB to Flutter
Entertainment/FLTR (2019-05-28), RBS to NatWest Group/NWG (2020-07-23), GVC Holdings/GVC to Entain/ENT (2020-12-09),
Reckitt Benckiser RB. to RKT (2021-04-01, TIDM only), Standard Life Aberdeen/SLA to abrdn/ABDN (2021-07-05), Royal
Dutch Shell/RDSB to Shell/SHEL (2022-01-31), Electrocomponents/ECM to RS Group/RS1 (2022-05-04), Intermediate Capital
ICP to ICG (2024-04-15, TIDM only), Barratt Developments/BDEV to Barratt Redrow/BTRW (2024-08-22) and Phoenix Group
Holdings/PHNX to Standard Life/SDLF (2026-03-02). Nine rest on a FTSE Russell notice, an SEC filing or a company RNS
and are unflagged; the remaining sixteen rest on company archives or press reporting, or have an approximate day, and
carry needs_verification. Two are TIDM changes with no change of legal name (Reckitt, ICG); one further legal-name
change is NOT represented because it moved no ticker - Intermediate Capital Group plc became ICG plc on 22 July 2025,
and this file keeps the earlier name under which FTSE Russell recorded the constituent.

TICKERS - THE WEAKEST FIELD IN THIS FILE. `needs_verification` on a change entry refers to the MEMBERSHIP FACT and its
date, not to the ticker. The BASE ticker for each company is an LSE TIDM/EPIC code supplied by the
author from knowledge and partially cross-checked against an EODHD LSE symbol list (live plus delisted); those base
codes carry NO primary citation and some are certainly wrong. What IS sourced is every ticker CHANGE: the 24 renames
above each cite the announcement that moved the code. Every ticker in this file is a real LSE code: the synthetic
placeholders an earlier revision used for two FTSE index-internal lines are gone with those entries. Do NOT resolve identifiers from these tickers without checking them; where a `sedol` is present it
came from the FTSE Russell review spreadsheet for THAT SAME effective date and is both point-in-time and the far
stronger identifier. 137 of the 464 member entries in `changes` carry a SEDOL on that basis; the rest do not, because
the review spreadsheet for their date was not recoverable, and no SEDOL has been carried across from a neighbouring
review. Anchor members carry no SEDOL at all: no FTSE Russell constituent file dated 19 December 2005 was recoverable,
and a SEDOL taken from a later review would not be point-in-time.

WHAT `needs_verification: true` MEANS HERE. It marks a change whose membership fact rests on the LSEG register alone,
with no second independent primary source (no recoverable review spreadsheet, no press release, no event-specific
notice). That is most of the ad-hoc events and the review quarters between December 2013 and December 2018, which is
the thinnest stretch of the file: FTSE Russell moved its review detail into login-gated attachments in December 2014
and LSEG's public press-release archive only starts in 2019, so for those quarters the register is usually the only
public record. Entries with `needs_verification: false` are corroborated by at least two of: the register, a review
spreadsheet, a press release, or an event-specific notice.

VALIDATION PERFORMED (all assertions passed). This file replays cleanly through
`trp.universe.sourcing.replay_index_history`, which is TICKER-keyed and strict: it rejects removing a non-member,
adding an existing member, renaming from a non-member or to an existing member, changes out of date order, a duplicate
anchor ticker, and any membership count outside 100 +/- 1. The replay yields 357 ticker spells, 100 of them open, and
those 100 open spells match the FTSE 100 constituents FTSE Russell published for the June 2026 review ticker for
ticker, with no differences in either direction. Additional throwaway assertions checked that no two entries share an
effective date, that every entry carries a non-empty `source`, that every `reason` is one of
review/acquisition/delisting/merger, that no added or removed member has an empty ticker, that no rename is a no-op,
that every review effective date is a Monday apart from the documented 26 March 2008 exception and falls after the
third Friday of the review month, and that the only dates on which the count leaves 100 are the four
demerger windows listed above. 248 distinct companies were members at some point in the span, of which 140 are no
longer in the index - the delisted, acquired and demoted names that a survivorship-free universe exists to retain. Name identity across renames was
resolved with an explicit alias table (for example Slough Estates -> SEGRO, Wolseley -> Ferguson, GVC Holdings ->
Entain, Phoenix Group Holdings -> Standard Life, Standard Life -> Standard Life Aberdeen -> abrdn -> Aberdeen Group);
that table is a modelling decision, not a source, and a consumer that resolves identifiers independently may disagree
with it.

RESOLVING THESE TICKERS AGAINST EODHD - READ BEFORE WIRING UP A LOADER. A price-coverage check of every ticker in this
file against EODHD's LSE history establishes two things a consumer must handle.
First, EODHD keys a company's WHOLE price history to its CURRENT code, not to the code in force at the time. Standard
Life/SL. and Standard Life Aberdeen/SLA return nothing, while ABDN returns a continuous series from 10 July 2006 - the
week of Standard Life's flotation - to today; African Barrick Gold/ABG returns nothing while Acacia Mining/ACA runs
from its March 2010 flotation; Reckitt's series is complete under RKT and stops in 2018 under RB. The point-in-time
codes in this file are correct and the provider's are not, so resolution must go through an effective-dated identifier
map rather than matching the provider's code directly.
Second, EODHD's delisted coverage does not reach a number of pre-2016 UK delistings at all. No series exists under any
code for SABMiller, Xstrata, Eurasian Natural Resources, Essar Energy, Autonomy, Cadbury, International Power,
Invensys, AMEC/Amec Foster Wheeler, ICAP, Friends Life, Worldpay Group or Home Retail Group. Two traps in that list:
Home Retail Group's genuine code HOME was later REUSED by the unrelated Home REIT (series 2020-2023), and HRG is Hogg
Robinson Group, not Home Retail; and WPY is the US-listed Worldpay Inc, whose series begins the day after Worldpay
Group left the index. Just Eat is a third kind of case - its price series stops on 24 December 2019 although its
membership runs to 5 February 2020, and that is a real market fact rather than a gap: FTSE Russell removed it 'using
the offer terms' because of 'the absence of an active market for Just Eat' (notice 2595355), having held it in the
index at a derived price through the delayed Takeaway.com scheme.

RECONCILIATION AGAINST EODHD, AND WHY IT DISAGREES. A cross-check of this file's end state against EODHD's live
`FTSE.INDX` component list on 16 August 2026 disagreed on three names in each direction: EODHD omitted Aberdeen
Group (ABDN), Computacenter (CCC) and Investec (INVP), and carried Berkeley Group (BKG), Mondi (MNDI) and Rightmove
(RMV). Those are exactly the six names of the June 2026 annual review recorded here effective 22 June 2026. The
disagreement was investigated and resolved AGAINST the provider; this file is unchanged, and a future reconciliation
will show the same difference until EODHD refreshes.
Evidence that the June 2026 review took effect as recorded: (i) FTSE Russell index notice 2620846, 3 June 2026, and
the LSEG press release of the same date, which name all six companies - the only amendment, notice 2620916 of 5 June
2026, concerns Home REIT in the FTSE SmallCap and leaves the FTSE 100 changes untouched; (ii) the Wikipedia 'FTSE 100
Index' constituent table as revised 31 July 2026, headed 'after the changes on 19 June 2026', which lists Aberdeen
Group, Computacenter and Investec and omits Berkeley, Mondi and Rightmove; (iii) the stockchallenge.co.uk FTSE
All-Share ranking as at the close on Thursday 13 August 2026, which tags ABDN, CCC and INVP as FTSE 100 and BKG, MNDI
and RMV as FTSE 250; and (iv) the Hargreaves Lansdown live FTSE 100 constituent listing
(https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-summary/ftse-100) read on 16 August 2026, which shows ABDN, CCC and INVP and
does not show BKG, MNDI or RMV.
Evidence that the provider snapshot is stale AND internally inconsistent, from the provider's own data: EODHD's
`FTMC.INDX` (FTSE 250) list on the same day contains ABDN, CCC and INVP - consistent with a snapshot taken before the
June 2026 review - but it ALSO contains IG Group (IGG) and Lion Finance Group (BGEO), which EODHD's `FTSE.INDX` list
simultaneously reports as FTSE 100 constituents. Those two were promoted at the March 2026 review, so EODHD's FTSE 100
list reflects March 2026 while its FTSE 250 list does not: the two lists are refreshed independently and are not a
coherent point-in-time pair. Neither endpoint carries an as-of timestamp. The practical warning: EODHD's UK index
component lists lag by an unknown and non-uniform amount and must not be used to date membership, nor treated as the
arbiter when they disagree with a FTSE Russell announcement.

KNOWN GAPS AND RESIDUAL RISK. (a) Ad-hoc events that the LSEG register omits AND that leave the constituent count
unchanged would be invisible to the replay; nothing guarantees the twelve repairs above are the only omissions, only
that they are the only ones the count and continuity tests could find. (b) Company names are as the source recorded
them and are not normalised across the file; the same company appears under different names before and after a rename,
and a `renamed` entry's `new_name` is the name in force at that date, not today's. (c) The rename list captures every
ticker change this file's own continuity requires plus every one the author could source for a continuously held
member; it is NOT a guaranteed-complete TIDM history, so a company whose code changed while it sat in the index
without the author noticing would still carry one code across that change. (d) Nothing here
covers the FTSE 250 or FTSE 350. (e) The file records membership only - no free-float weights, no shares in issue, no
index weights. (f) The period before 19 December 2005 is not covered even though the LSEG register reaches back to
1984, because no full constituent snapshot was sourced for an earlier anchor date.
